column1: # The rung-3 engine facts: standing rules, not requirements.
# These were written as requirements m3 and m4 and were demoted here after item
# 4.3 measured them. The measurement, which is the whole reason this file exists
#   At this step the runtime is the *verifier image's* Spark, not the pom's.
#   spark-core is `provided` scope, the jar is shaded without it, and the
#   replay's spark-submit is /opt/spark/bin/spark-submit -- which is 3.2.4 in
#   step 3's image whatever `<spark.version>` says. So the tree that changed
#   nothing was replayed at 3.2.4 and reported conf=true, adaptiveUpdate 2/6/2/2
#   over four of five sampled jobs, and statisticalAggregate=false -- the same
#   five facts the golden tree reports. Graded as requirements they paid a
#   do-nothing tree 0.14 for the image's version number.
# A requirement no candidate can fail prices nothing, so they stopped being
# requirements. What they actually measured was two different things, and round
# 1 of the item-5 review was right that one file could not carry both:
#   a precondition   the reading happened on an engine where the 3.1 and 3.2
#                    semantics are in force and the optimiser really ran. If one
#                    of these is FAIL the run is not the run this step grades,
#                    and the migrated family voids rather than losing a share.
#                    That is what is left in this file.
#   a prohibition    the tree, or the way it was submitted, switched one of
#                    those semantics back off. Both agent-visible documents
#                    price that as a faked step -- worth nothing at all,
#                    requirements and behaviour alike -- and a standing rule
#                    cannot charge that, because it leaves behaviour standing.
#                    Those four moved to rules/cheats3.tsv, which is the file
#                    score.py reads for prohibitions.
# What did NOT get demoted with any of them is the thing they stood for. The 3.1
# statistical-aggregate change is still graded, through the replay: stddev over
# a single-row group renders NaN at 3.0.3 and null at 3.2.4, and c04 -- the
# reference census -- carries the 3.2.4 value in AnalyzeWaterInteractions4. A
# tree that forced the legacy semantics back on fails the replay family on its
# own output. The step stopped paying twice for one fact; it did not stop
# measuring it.
# Included from step 3 onward and not from common.tsv, because every one of
# these is false at steps 1 and 2 by construction: 3.0.3 has adaptive execution
# off by default and does not have the statisticalAggregate key at all.
rung3-adaptive-on
column5: no replayed job ran with adaptive query execution enabled; at this runtime that is the default, so this reading was not taken on the engine this step grades

column1: rung3-adaptive-acting
column5: the optimiser never reported re-planning a query across the whole replay, so adaptive execution was switched on and never did anything -- the setting is a fact about the version, and only the re-plan is a fact about the run

column1: rung3-stat-aggregate-modern
column5: no replayed job ran with Spark 3.1 statistical-aggregate semantics in force; stddev over a single-row group would still render NaN
